feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration 10 design, which is the best raced design (score 60.27 against 54.14 for the next best). It differs from iteration 6 only in sensor y, moved from 0.03 to 0.06, and base_speed is 1.25. Iteration 10 showed the gain came mainly from oval progress (0.163 against 0.118), oval rms_error (0.0194 against 0.0293) and oval control effort (1.24 against 1.92). Progress on the s-bend and slalom was unchanged, and every track still has one line-loss event per trial with max_error of about 0.063 m. So the excursion is not solved, but forward placement is the only lever that has moved the score. Iterations 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9 each left the excursion unchanged, which rules out spacing, ki, kd, recovery direction, kp and footprint as the main limit. The candidate is valid (y = 0.06 is inside the 0.08 limit), it matches the best raced evidence, and it is the final race, so no later iteration can correct it. Extending y to 0.08 is an untested single step with unproven benefit on an unseen track, and it risks the one result we have measured. Approve the best-measured design.
requested_changes: No change is requested: approve the iteration 10 design as raced (base_speed 1.25, kp 1.5, ki 0, kd 0.15, last_direction, sensors at x = +0.03, +0.015, 0, -0.015, -0.03 with y = 0.06, 16 mm footprints), because it is the best raced evidence (60.27 against 54.14).

For the record, the unseen-track race will show whether forward placement holds outside the development tracks; judge the result on max_error, line_loss_events and progress per track, as the iteration 10 telemetry did.
